opus.why: Review of a billing PR of unknown size. Mistakes cost money, so it needs Opus-level bug finding, but it's one routine PR, so medium effort is enough.

fable.why: Open-ended review of a billing-API PR of unknown scope. Money logic is where missed subtle bugs cost the most, so opus-level judgment is needed; medium effort suffices for reading a diff and reasoning about it.

opus.why: Multi-repo cross review: run parallel reviewer subagents, then check their findings for contradictions and merge them. The orchestration and judgment need Opus at high effort.

fable.why: Multi-repo payment-ticket cross review: orchestrate two subagents, then adjudicate real contradictions between their findings and produce one merged list. Long agentic task with judgment-heavy reconciliation on payment code; the user also explicitly asks for high thinking.

opus.why: Security review of a short auth diff. The flaws are fairly clear: decode is used instead of verify, exp is compared in the wrong units (seconds vs ms), the token is logged, the stack trace leaks, and the role comes from a header. Sonnet at high effort catches all of these reliably.

fable.why: Security review of a 30-line auth diff. The bugs (decode instead of verify, token logging, stack leak, x-role header bypass, query-token fallback, exp seconds-vs-ms) are textbook; sonnet at high catches them all with no quality loss, and security warrants not going lower.

opus.why: Check of one commit (an upload endpoint) for obvious problems. Upload security has standard checks (path traversal, file type, size) that Sonnet at high effort covers well.

fable.why: Review one commit for an asset upload endpoint, scoped to 'anything obviously wrong'. Needs repo reading and standard upload-security checks (path traversal, type/size validation, auth); sonnet high handles this fully.

opus.why: Follow-up: a light sanity pass after the fixes, then commit messages that summarize work already done. Both are routine.

fable.why: Explicitly lighter sanity pass over already-fixed findings plus writing commit messages summarizing them. Verification of known fixes and summarization, not fresh deep review; sonnet high is enough.

opus.why: Small single-file queue script. The bugs are standard: no lock so two workers can grab the same clip, a None job when the queue is empty, MAX_RETRIES never enforced, shell injection, crashed jobs stuck as running, no atomic writes. Sonnet at high effort finds them all.

fable.why: Small Python file with clear concurrency and edge-case bugs (None job on empty queue, no file locking between workers, MAX_RETRIES never enforced, stuck 'running' on crash, shell injection). Sonnet at high reasons through these reliably.

opus.why: Full branch review focused on concurrent use of one promo code and what happens to it when an order is cancelled. Money logic plus race conditions needs deep reasoning, so Opus at high effort.

fable.why: Branch-vs-main review of promo-code logic requiring reasoning about race conditions (two users applying the same code concurrently) and order-cancellation state transitions across a real codebase. Concurrency correctness plus money; opus high is needed to catch subtle missed cases.

opus.why: The review comments get posted on GitHub where other people read them, in a set format. Comment quality and accuracy matter, but it's one PR, so Opus at medium effort.

fable.why: Review a mobile-app PR and post inline GitHub comments in a strict format. Outward-facing comments and strict instruction following, but ordinary review scope; sonnet high does this as well as opus.

opus.why: Production migration on 8M rows. It loses middle names and other name parts, drops the column irreversibly, holds a long lock in one transaction, builds the index without CONCURRENTLY, and its rollback is lossy. The risk is high, but the scope is one SQL file.

fable.why: Pre-prod migration review on an 8M-row table. The issues are well-known patterns: split_part drops middle names, irreversible DROP in the same transaction, long-held locks from a single big UPDATE and non-concurrent index, broken rollback. Sonnet high identifies all of them and recommends batching/concurrent index without loss versus opus.
